payload.text: EVERY cargo gate reaches every member of the workspace it claims to gate, and the population comes from the manifest rather than from the command's default or from a hand-written list. AC-1.9 stated this correctly for cargo test and scoped it to cargo test, which is the enumeration error one level up: the property is about GATES, and test is one of several. THE ROW THEN MADE THE SAME ERROR ONE LEVEL DOWN -- it named two homes and said "all three gates", and the estate has SIX SITES IN THREE FILES, measured 2026-09-09 by vc and cc independently at pickup. cargo test: --workspace, fixed in WP-01. cargo clippy in CI: had no --workspace, so a member crate's TEST code was never linted and one real lint sat behind it -- found and fixed by cc in 8dea619. THE OTHER FIVE ARE LIVE. (1) CI's per-crate release build in tests.yml, which is the line DIRECTLY ABOVE the comment explaining why --workspace is required -- the comment is attached to the cargo test call beneath it and reads "--workspace or every crate but the root package is silently skipped", describing the call above it exactly. (2) The shim's build in prez_ensure_built. (3) acceptance.sh's AT12 clippy arm, the check labelled "clippy warnings and errors", which the suite's own comment calls the load-bearing gate: it is 8dea619's defect still live, and artifact and showreel are unlinted by it today. (4) AT01's release build, legitimately prez-scoped since AT01 asserts prez's own binary and its 8 MB ceiling -- correct now, listed because a later AT needing the showreel binary makes it wrong silently. (5) The unconditional pre-build between AT01 and AT02, which every later AT depends on. AND THE SIXTH IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM WITH NO FLAG TO FIX IT, cc's find, verified from source by vc: prez_is_stale's find -newer walk enumerates src, themes, assets, the manifest and Cargo.lock, and NOT crates -- so an edit to any member crate leaves the shim reporting the binary current and it never rebuilds. Silent: no message, no failure, an old binary. Its comment names this exact class, saying a watcher over src alone would report a stale binary as current, which is why themes and assets were added; crates joined the workspace later and the walk was not extended. SO THE POPULATION HAS TWO MECHANISMS AND ONE FIX DOES NOT COVER BOTH -- five take their population from cargo's default and one flag reaches them; the sixth takes it from a typed directory list and no flag reaches it. A sweep that adds --workspace everywhere and stops leaves the silent one, which is the worse of the two. TWICE NOW THE KNOWLEDGE WAS PRESENT AT THE SITE AND DID NOT PREVENT THE DEFECT: CI carries the explanation one line from the violation, and the shim carries the class description directly above the walk that commits it. That is the argument for taking the population from the manifest rather than restating the rule in a comment. Discharged when every gate takes its population from the manifest by both mechanisms, driven and shown to disagree with the unscoped form.
